# Compute w_0 at eta using mass constraint m_0 = w_0 + sum(w_i) [S1, G]

The claim states that $w_0$ is computed at $eta$ using the mass constraint $m_0 = w_0 + sum(w_i)$. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly defines the evaluation point as $x_0 = eta$ (Section 3.1, paragraph 2: 'because $x_0 = eta$ is given'). It further states that the moments satisfy the system $m_k = sum_{i=0}^n w_i x_i^k$ (Eq. 12). For the zeroth moment ($k=0$), this equation becomes $m_0 = sum_{i=0}^n w_i x_i^0 = w_0 + sum_{i=1}^n w_i$. Thus, the evidence supports the claim that the mass constraint $m_0 = w_0 + sum(w_i)$ is used to relate the weights, including $w_0$ at $eta$.
